articles.title: Alex Pereira reta a Ciryl Gane y pide una revancha por el título del peso pesado
articles.standfirst: Ante la ausencia prolongada de Tom Aspinall, campeón indiscutido, 'Poatan' quiere una oportunidad de redimirse ante el francés
articles.summary: Ante la ausencia prolongada de Tom Aspinall, campeón indiscutido, 'Poatan' quiere una oportunidad de redimirse ante el francés
articles.body: Alex Pereira fue otro de los grandes derrotados del UFC Casa Blanca del pasado 14 de junio. 'Poatan' debutó en peso pesado ante Ciryl Gane por el cinturón interino, y una victoria le hubiese convertido en el primer peleador de la historia en conseguir el título en tres categorías diferentes. Sin embargo, no fue la noche del brasileño y el peleador francés le acabó noqueando para evitar que cumpliese su sueño. Aún así, Pereira no ha quedado conforme con el resultado, y ante la ausencia prolongada de Tom Aspinall -campeón indiscutido- ha pedido una oportunidad de revancha ante el galo. La situación en el peso pesado es muy complicada. En octubre de 2025 Aspinall y Gane se midieron en un combate que acabó en un 'No Contest' -sin resultado- por un doble piquete de ojo de Ciryl en el primer asalto. Lo que parecía una situación aislada que no iría a mayores acabó con una grave lesión ocular del inglés, que se ha tenido que someter a varias operaciones y no ha podido pelear desde entonces. Además, en este lapso de tiempo Tom se ha unido a Eddie Hearn -promotor de boxeo rival de Dana White-, lo que ha generado aún más tensión entre él y la UFC. Por otro lado está Pereira, que se quejó de su derrota con Gane por recibir varios golpes ilegales en la nuca durante la pelea, llegando a pedir el despido de Herb Dean -árbitro del combate-. Parecían que las aguas se habían calmado, pero 'Poatan' ha vuelto a aparecer en escena para retar a Gane. "El combate que tiene sentido es el de Ciryl Gane. Ese es el combate, voy a trabajar en ello. Y por lo que veo, es algo que va a suceder", afirmó en sus redes sociales. Se rumoreaba que Pereira podría incluso pelear contra Josh Hokit para ver quién era el próximo contendiente al cinturón, pero la situación de Aspinall ha provocado un cambio de planes. El peleador inglés ha revelado que quizás tenga que volver a someterse a otra operación, por lo que no sería de extrañar que la UFC le obligue a dejar el cinturón vacante dentro de poco. Esto convertiría a Gane, hasta ahora campeón interino, en campeón indiscutido, y una revancha contra Pereira sería lo más lógico. Es cierto que el peleador francés se mostró muy superior a Alex, pero la falta de nombres mediáticos dentro de la parte alta de la categoría y la necesidad de la promotora de generar supercombates les deja en una tesitura complicada. Ya ha habido muchas críticas tras el anuncio del UFC 332, por lo que la compañía no se puede permitir otro evento numerado fallido. Ambos peleadores están sanos y salieron sin lesiones, por lo que un duelo entre ambos para finales de año o para inicios de 2027 sería un gran aliciente para cualquier cartelera. El tiempo dirá.

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Briton Conor Benn 'dragged down to pits of hell' by weight cut
articles.summary: Conor Benn says making the welterweight limit for his world-title challenge against Ryan Garcia has felt like being "dragged down to the pits of hell" but insists he is healthy and will make weight.
articles.body:
Conor Benn says making the welterweight limit for his world title challenge against Ryan Garcia has felt like being "dragged down to the pits of hell" but insists he is healthy and will make weight.

Benn, 29, faces WBC champion Garcia at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Saturday in the first world title fight of his 10-year professional career.

The Briton must weigh no more than 10st 7lb (67kg) when he steps on the scales in on Friday, having not made the welterweight limit for more than four years.

"It's been extremely difficult," Benn told BBC Sport.

"It feels like I've been dragged down to the pits of hell, had a fight with Satan and God brought me back to life.

"Making weight has been the hardest thing I've done. I haven't made weight for four and a half years so it's going to be hard.

"But I won't moan when I'm getting paid a fortune to headline in Vegas for a world title. I know what I signed up for."

Benn last made the welterweight limit when stopping Chris van Heerden in two rounds in April 2022.

He stepped up to 11st 6lb (73kg) for two lucrative contests with Chris Eubank Jr last year, suffering the first defeat of his professional career in April 2025 before avenging the loss on points seven months later.

'Healthy' Benn would vacate world title 'straight away'

Benn's appearance in pictures and videos posted on social media during fight week has prompted concern among some observers over the effects of dropping back to welterweight.

Former world champion Carl Froch and Benn's former opponent Chris Algieri are among those to have questioned whether the weight cut could leave him depleted.

It is particularly pertinent given the contrasting styles on Saturday. Benn is an aggressive, front-foot fighter who likes to apply pressure, while American Garcia, 28, possesses fast hands and is renowned for a dangerous counter left hook.

But Benn dismissed concerns over his condition.

"I'm healthy," he said, adding that he expects to rehydrate significantly and enter the ring at around 12st 7lb (80kg) - two stones heavier than the welterweight limit.

Even if he fulfils a lifelong ambition by winning a maiden world title and following in his father Nigel's footsteps, Benn intends to vacate the belt "straight away" and move back up to middleweight or potentially as high as super-middleweight.

"I love challenges and that's what life is about, otherwise it's boring," he added.

For all the difficulty presented by the weight cut, there was little outward sign of Benn being weighed down by the occasion.

He was relaxed and in good spirits as he made time for the travelling British media at the UFC's Meta Apex, with father and British boxing great Nigel Benn by his side.

The former two-weight world champion has been a prominent presence throughout fight week, despite previously suggesting he would take a step back from his son's career.

One man Conor Benn is yet to see, however, is his opponent.

Garcia did not appear for a scheduled face-off at Mandalay Bay on Tuesday, with Benn told beforehand that the champion would not be attending.

Benn turned up regardless and jokingly squared up to his 62-year-old father instead.

He described Garcia as a "strange geezer" and said the no-show had done the champion "no favours".

"I'm not bothered, I've dealt with worse," Conor Benn added. "If he turns up or not, it makes no difference to me.

"Irrespective of how hard the weight cut is or anything else, we owe it to the public to give the fans what they want. It's a lack of discipline and professionalism."

articles.summary: Wednesday's Dynamite was already planned to be the special Rebel Hearts episode to benefit ALS research, but it also turned into a tribute to the late Andy Williams.
articles.body:
Wednesday's Dynamite was already planned to be the special Rebel Hearts episode to benefit ALS research, but it also turned into a tribute to the late Andy Williams.

Known to AEW fans as The Butcher, Williams was also a prolific guitarist and a beloved talent by all who knew him.

Wednesday's episode included a special edition of The Waiting Room with Rebel and Britt Baker in addition to all of the usual action.

Let's take a look at what happened on this week's Dynamite.

Dynamite opened with a graphic paying tribute to Andy Williams as the crowd could be heard chanting Butcher's name. Excalibur ran down the card for the night before we went to The Waiting Room.

Rebel introduced Britt Baker for the segment. They shared a cute moment before bringing out Persephone, who bragged about being a double champion in AEW and CMLL.

They also welcomed Hikaru Shida, whom Baker still held responsible for breaking her nose back in the day. This wasn't a very long segment, but it accomplished what it set out to do.

Seeing Rebel smiling and enjoying herself was the best part.

Baker doing the old Reba/Rebel joke while telling Rebel how brave she is was a very sweet moment.

Bringing up how Shida broke Baker's nose was funny.

The New Level and Swerve Strickland vs. The Conglomeration (Trios Titles)

Last time in action: The New Level and Swerve Strickland defeated The Conglomeration and everyone else (All In)

The first match of the night saw Swerve Strickland, Kofi and Austin Creed defend the Trios Championships against Orange Cassidy, Roderick Strong and Kyle O'Reilly.

Swerve and Cassidy started, but the crowd seemed more excited to see KOR and Creed tag in. They traded some kicks to the thigh as they tried to one-up each other, but it was Creed who came out on top.

Strong using Cassidy as a weapon was one of the best parts of the match, but all six men put in some great work. The least surprising thing about this was that it was entertaining.

The trios titles felt a bit directionless in the first half of 2026, so it's great to see Swerve and The New Level starting their reign with some strong title defenses.

This was a typical AEW trios bout. It was a back-and-forth fight with everyone getting a little time to shine. Both teams looked strong, but the ending was definitely predictable. After an exciting final sequence, the champions scored the win when New Level hit Daybreak on OC for the pin.

Result: Swerve and The New Level defeated The Conglomeration

Giving The New Level a licensed song was cool, but it would be nice to hear what Mikey Rukus could come up with for their music.

The standoff between Swerve and OC was funny.

Strong throwing Cassidy around like a weapon was a great sequence.

Kofi and Creed have some of the best double-team offense. Everything is so smooth after working together for so long.

The look of disgust on Swerve's face with OC hit the slow kicks was priceless.

articles.title: Roberto Soldic admits UFC pay 'not even close' to ONE deal after 'depressing' stint on sidelines
articles.summary: Soldic, 31, signed with ONE Championship as a marquee free agent in 2021. He ended up wasting nearly a half-decade of his prime years stuck in no-man's land.
articles.body:
Roberto Soldic is finally set to arrive in the UFC. But it didn't come without spending several precious prime years of his career stuck on the sidelines.

Prior to his recent UFC signing, Soldic was with ONE Championship in Asia , having joined the promotion in 2021 as one of the hottest free agents in MMA after years of dominance in Poland's KSW promotion as a two-weight champion. When Soldic signed with ONE, he did so on a monster deal that came with big promises attached. Speaking on Wednesday's edition of "The Ariel Helwani Show," Soldic acknowledged that his ONE contract was far more lucrative than his new UFC contract, and that it's "not even close."

Even during Soldic's 2021 free agency, the initial offer UFC presented him had a bit more financial incentive than what he ended up accpeting in 2026.

"I'm happy," Soldic told Uncrowned. "I think I had the best offer [the first time] as a fighter before deciding. I can say this. I had a very good offer, but ONE was a little bit bigger offer.

"I took this chance to go in ONE because they promised me I could do some kickboxing stuff, Muay Thai stuff, so I liked this. They offered me 10 fights, but I [ended up doing] only three. Contract expired. It is what it is. I'm happy now with the UFC. It's a good offer, and I want to stay here."

Soldic, 31, isn't the first high-profile MMA fighter under the ONE banner to depart the company in 2026 due to activity-related frustrations. He ultimately fought just three times in nearly five years with ONE, and only once since May 2023.

Soldic wishes he could have seen his initial expectations met from his 10-fight deal, though he acknowledges that he never experienced issues with his financial treatment on the rare occasions he was able to actually secure opportunities to fight.

"They pay always on time. I don't have any trouble with the payments," Soldic said. "I don't know what's going on with ONE. I think they like more striking fights in Japan and in Thailand, and there are really, really good guys there as strikers.

"[But] I don't know what's happened with MMA [in ONE] — I know so many guys left ONE as MMA fighters. And kickboxing is also on the highest level [in the promotion], and Muay Thai. But … as a fighter, before in ONE Championship, I can say everything was on time when they paid me, so I don't know what's happening. I don't think it's a financial situation, but [the] media is writing everything [about the promotion's ongoing troubles], so, who knows?"

At UFC 332 on Oct. 3 in Salt Lake City, Soldic makes his long-awaited UFC debut at welterweight opposite Khaos Williams. It will be his first MMA fight since February 2025.

In the meantime, Soldic did his best to stay active, defeating Tomasz Adamek via second-round TKO in a boxing match with Polish organization Fame one year ago.

Soldic said he doesn't have any regrets about signing with ONE, but admitted he was frustrated throughout his time there, missing out on seven fights he was promised.

"It's more frustrating that I stayed, like, semi-retired," Soldic said. "This was the most frustrating. It's hard to deal with because I train hard always, always in shape, and I just didn't get a fight. Sometimes I asked myself, why I train so hard when I don't have a fight?

"It was a hard time, a little bit depressing, but I stayed strong and am moving forward."

articles.title: Dana White’s blunt words on Ilia Topuria reveal what could come next for his UFC return
articles.summary: MMA News: Ilia Topuria’s UFC comeback may be much closer than expected, and Dana White has now given the clearest update yet. The UFC CEO confirmed that the for.
articles.body: Ilia Topuria’s UFC comeback may be much closer than expected, and Dana White has now given the clearest update yet. The UFC CEO confirmed that the former lightweight champion is ready to return, despite the serious injuries he suffered in his loss to Justin Gaethje. Topuria’s recovery had already created hope that he could fight again before the end of 2026. White’s latest comments take that optimism a step further. The UFC is ready for him, but his next opponent has not been decided. For now, both Gaethje and Paddy Pimblett remain possible options.Dana White confirms Ilia Topuria is ready as the UFC waits for his next moveDana White has made it clear that the UFC is not holding Topuria back from competition. Speaking to Jim Rome, White explained that the promotion remains in contact with the former champion and is prepared to move forward when the right fight is available."Our guys are always in touch with them. We don't have him on the schedule right now, but listen, Topuria's ready to fight. We're ready for him."That statement is significant because Topuria’s return looked far less certain immediately after his latest fight.The 29-year-old suffered his first professional loss against Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250. The defeat ended his unbeaten run and came with serious physical damage. Reports indicated fractures to both orbital bones, along with injuries to his nose and foot.Those injuries initially raised the possibility of a lengthy absence. A return in 2027 was even discussed.The recovery process, however, has moved faster than expected.Topuria’s strength and conditioning coach Jesus Gallo previously suggested that the former champion could potentially return before the end of 2026. Topuria has also dropped hints about his next appearance, giving fans more reason to believe his comeback is approaching.White’s latest comments now provide the strongest indication yet that the UFC is preparing for that return.The key point is that Topuria does not have a fight officially booked. That leaves the UFC with an important decision over who should welcome him back.Dana White sees big opportunities in both a Gaethje rematch and a Paddy Pimblett fightDana White appears to have two major options in mind for Topuria.One is a rematch with Gaethje. The other is a long-awaited showdown with Paddy Pimblett.When Jim Rome asked White which fight he preferred, the UFC CEO did not commit to either matchup."[Justin Gaethje or Paddy Pimblett?] Both sound good to me. They're both great. We don't lose with either one of those fights. They're both great fights; I don't know."A second fight with Gaethje would give Topuria an immediate chance to respond to the biggest setback of his career. Their first meeting was not decided by a controversial scorecard. Gaethje gradually took control before Topuria’s corner stopped the fight ahead of the fifth round.That makes a rematch easy to understand from a storyline perspective. Topuria would have the opportunity to correct what went wrong and show whether he can handle Gaethje differently the second time.Pimblett offers another kind of attraction.The two lightweight stars have built a heated rivalry over several years. Their relationship has included repeated verbal attacks and confrontations, giving a potential fight plenty of tension before the opening bell.White acknowledged that history while discussing the matchup."They're both great; we don't have anything set… I don't really have the answer to that question. I mean, obviously the rematch with Gaethje is incredible. And a Paddy Pimblett fight is amazing. You know, as bad as those two hate each other."There is also a sporting question surrounding the Gaethje rematch. Topuria lost the lightweight title without successfully defending it, while Gaethje has argued that another contender should have a stronger claim to the next championship opportunity.That could make an immediate rematch difficult to justify from a rankings standpoint.Still, White’s comments show that the idea remains alive.For now, the biggest takeaway is not which opponent Topuria will face. It is that the UFC boss believes the former champion is ready to return.Dana White has effectively moved the conversation forward. Topuria’s comeback is no longer simply being discussed as a future possibility. The UFC is preparing for it, and the next decision could determine whether he returns looking for revenge against Gaethje or settles his long-running rivalry with Pimblett.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: American reveals why he snubbed face-off, as Brit says he 'went through hell' to make weight
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia was criticised by Conor Benn after he failed to show up for a face-off with the British fighter on Tuesday, ahead of their much-anticipated WBC welterweight showdown in Las Vegas on Saturday
articles.body:
Garcia is set to embark on the first defence of his WBC welterweight title against Benn at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Saturday night.

Earlier in the week, the pair were due to meet at the Mandalay Bay Hotel for a media event, but the American fighter did not show up, with Benn subsequently claiming his opponent had "bottled it".

During a press conference on Wednesday, Garcia said: "I wasn't there because I didn't want to be.

"Look, we have a face-off at the press conference [Thursday], then at the weigh-ins [Friday] and then a final face-off literally in the ring when the refs give you instructions.

"I've been doing this for so long. I've had fight weeks in Vegas before. I've never had to do a face-off on [Tuesday]. So I have a routine to do, and it's just something I didn't want to do.''

"It was funny seeing him [Benn] staring at himself."

Benn, meanwhile, believes Garcia's absence let the fans down.

"Ultimately it's disrespectful to the public because they deserve it,'' he said on Wednesday.

"The public deserves us giving you guys the best. This is what we do. This is what we're here for.''

Benn: Weight cut dragged me through the pits of hell

Benn comes into this fight as the underdog after stepping up to middleweight to fight Chris Eubank Jr. He lost his first fight against his rival in April 2025, before avenging that loss later that November. He comes into this weekend's bout after beating Regis Prograis at a 150lbs catchweight in April.

Should Benn make the weight at Friday's weigh-in, this will be the first time that he has fought at the welterweight limit in over four years, with his last fight at under 147lbs coming against Chris van Heerden in April 2022.

The 29-year-old hit back at those who have doubted his ability to make the weight, but added he felt like he had been "dragged through the pits of hell and had a fight with satan" during his preparations.

"A lot of people said I couldn't make the weight, watch me do it," Benn said, adding he went through 15 weeks of dieting before the fight.

Benn added that this would be his last fight at 147lbs and is hoping to move up in weight after this to 160 or 168lbs.

Garcia said he didn't want to hear any excuses from Benn after the fight regarding his weight cut.

"All we can do is go by past experience," Garcia said. "He cut back down to 150lbs to fight Regis Prograis. We have seen how he bloated up. Now he has an extra three pounds to go. I don't want to hear any excuses. He doesn't have a rehydration clause.

"I don't want to be hearing any crybaby s*** from him. He's trying to set up a narrative, because when he gets his a** whopped, he'll say: 'I was drained'. I'm about to beat his a**, it doesn't matter how much he weighs."

articles.title: Garcia vs Benn: Ryan Garcia says Conor Benn does not deserve world title shot
articles.summary: Ryan Garcia says Conor Benn is nothing more than an "average fighter" and does not deserve a shot at his WBC welterweight title.
articles.body:
Ryan Garcia says Conor Benn is nothing more than an "average fighter" and that the Briton does not deserve a shot at his WBC welterweight title.

Garcia, 28, makes the first defence of his belt against Benn at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas on Saturday.

The American has consistently dismissed Benn's ability during the build-up and, after skipping Tuesday's face-off, has been accused overlooking the 29-year-old.

But Garcia says he is not taking anything lightly as he aims for a 26th win in 29 bouts as a professional.

Asked whether Benn, who has not fought at welterweight since April 2022, deserves the opportunity to challenge for a world title, Garcia said: "Not at all."

He told BBC Sport: "He's an average fighter, he's athletic and it's his last name. It's not a shot at him; it's just the bitter truth.

"I'm preparing like he's the best fighter in the world. It's all about preparation and how sharp you are.

"People could say you're overlooking him. No, I'm calling it how I see it.

"Do you want me to say he's as good as Floyd Mayweather? He's not.

"He's alright. He comes forward and throws looping overhands. He's aggressive and will make him a rugged fight, but it's not something I haven't seen before."

Garcia and Benn have documented their fight camps on social media, but have presented their preparations in different ways.

Benn has posted videos of his training regime, while Garcia has been collaborating with influencers and making appearances in the WWE.

"He's not my cup of tea. I wouldn't want to hang out with him too much," Garcia said.

"He's a bit of a hypocrite and contradicts himself a lot. I am who I am - goofy and outgoing, making jokes and having fun.

"He is trying to say he's humble, but he's out here any chance in a Rolls Royce. He loves the lights.

"He thinks I'm like that, but I'm focused on my craft 100%."

articles.title: La desgracia familiar que forjó el carácter de Jean Silva, la estrella de UFC Noche
articles.standfirst: El peleador brasileño se medirá en el combate estelar a José Delgado, y tiene una historia detrás que ha marcado su forma de ser
articles.summary: El peleador brasileño se medirá en el combate estelar a José Delgado, y tiene una historia detrás que ha marcado su forma de ser
articles.body: Este sábado 12 de septiembre, la UFC hará tributo al pueblo mexicano otro año más con UFC Noche, con Jean Silva (17-3) enfrentándose a José Delgado (12-2) en el combate estelar. En un principio, 'Lord' se tenía que medir a Yair Rodríguez, pero una lesión de 'El Pantera' ha dejado en una difícil situación a una de las mayores superestrellas de peso pluma, que tiene un carácter díscolo marcado por las desgracias familiares que vivió de pequeño. Silva se crió en la favelas de Brasil, y le tocó vivir la crudeza del barrio como a cualquier niño que vive en esos ambientes. El primer evento traumático que le marcó de por vida fue ver cómo tres hombres abusaban sexualmente de su madre, y más tarde ella cogía un cuchillo y los asesinaba. Cada vez que lo recuerda rompe en llanto, ya que a su corta edad no podía entender cómo había tanta maldad en el mundo. Otro sello de identidad de Jean son esos ladridos constantes que hace imitando a un perro desde el inicio de la Fight Week hasta que entra al octágono. También tienen un trasfondo detrás, igual de cruel que su primera historia. El hermano de Jean le regaló un perro en su adolescencia, y comenzó a imitar sus ladridos constantemente. Al tiempo, Silva tuvo que ver cómo asesinaban a su hermano en la favela, en otro momento traumático de su vida que la persigue desde entonces. De ahí que el carácter de 'Lord' sea tan complicado de entender. Impredecible y alocado en su personalidad, pero muy calculador cuando entra al octágono, lo que le ha permitido quedarse a las puertas del cinturón de peso pluma. Es cierto que el año pasado vio frenado su ascenso con un codazo giratorio de Diego Lopes que supuso su primera derrota en la compañía, pero se ha repuesto de la mejor manera ganando a Arnold Allen el pasado enero. Una victoria ante Yair Rodríguez le habría asegurado un combate titular ante el ganador del duelo entre Alexander Volkanovski y Movsar Evloev del próximo UFC 333, pero el nuevo escenario que se le ha presentado es bastante menos esperanzador. José Delgado acaba de entrar en el top 15 de la división, por lo que una victoria ante él sería lo lógico y posiblemente no le asegure nada. Además, si pierde será un batacazo muy duro para su carrera, por lo que la presión está sobre sus hombros. Delgado es un striker peligroso que puede dar la sorpresa y que no tiene nada que perder, y tiene el aliciente extra de contar con el apoyo del pueblo mexicano. Si logra dar la machada será él el que se quede cerca del cinturón, en una oportunidad de oro que le ha caído de la nada y que intentara aprovechar al máximo para seguir avanzando en su carrera.

articles.title: B/R Staff Predictions for Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn
articles.summary: Will "King Ry" get dethroned by a British boxer with a rich pedigree?
articles.body:
Will "King Ry" get dethroned by a British boxer with a rich pedigree?

That is the question that must be answered on Saturday night in Las Vegas, as Ryan Garcia defends his WBC welterweight title against Conor Benn.

Benn is the son of former world champion Nigel Benn and will attempt to join his father as a championship holder.

The B/R Combat Sports staff got together to provide predictions for the big fight in Vegas.

It's never good when a fighter heads into a bout already looking to the future.

Conor Benn has admitted his weight cut was "brutal" and that this will be his last outing at 147 pounds. That won't do anything to hush the detractors who think Ryan Garcia will have an easy time putting the Englishman away with the 21st knockout of his career.

I'll say this about Benn: A defeat wouldn't be through a lack of effort. He's exactly the type of fighter who can give Garcia issues. He won't be afraid to pull up close and get among it. We saw in his second fight against Chris Eubank Jr. that he also holds legit power in the latter rounds, sending his British rival to the deck twice in Round 12. Garcia needs to take him seriously.

That's likely to be the defining point of this showdown. Garcia will make Benn's life a living hell if he turns up with the confidence that saw him dominate Mario Barrios. Should we see the Garcia who lost to Rolando Romero, there's a good chance Benn could capitalize. Garcia became timid after getting hurt early against Romero, a blueprint the underdog should look to repeat.

With that said, I think Garcia gets it done. Benn has already endured a demanding camp and weight cut, and he's facing a man who is motivated to remind people why he's considered such an elite talent. I can see a late knockout after the wear and tear sets in.

Conor Benn rarely goes quietly, which is part of what makes this fight compelling.

The goal should be to pressure Garcia with a high work rate and the constant threat of sustained offense. In doing so, Benn will try to play the short and long game—depleting energy throughout and adding to the mental exhaustion of keeping a fighter on their heels for many minutes.

If we were coaching Benn, this style would have to stay intact. Win or lose, he must stay true to an aggressive fighting style that has earned him a 25-1 record. In particular, he has a real shot at flipping this fight in the first few rounds. His efforts here could pave the way for a long night for his opponent.

Garcia, of course, is well aware of this. He's the faster fighter, a brilliant counterpuncher, and still extremely explosive. In many respects, this is the kind of fight that suits his fighting style. The only difference is that most opponents don't hit as hard and fight as well as Benn does.

Others have made the point, but it can't be stated enough: weight will be a factor. Benn has publicly acknowledged this weight cut as "brutal," and he plans to move to 168 pounds after this 147-pound fight. Energy, which is one of his best attributes, should be a concern.

You never quite know how these dramatic cuts will impact a fight, but they will have a say one way or another.

This fight, however, still feels much more about Garcia's boxing and skill evolution than anything else. Regardless of how smoothly Benn's weight cut goes, he will be ready. The opening rounds will be exciting and violent.

It'll be up to Garcia to avoid carnage and take over with speed and tactical shots as the fight progresses, and he should be able to do just that.

Let's face it. I should really stay out of the Ryan Garcia picks business.

I was pretty sure Devin Haney would embarrass him when they met two years ago in Brooklyn—right up until "King Ry" bounced "The Dream" like a ball. Garcia's subsequent positive tests for ostarine led the result to be changed to a no-contest.

Then, last spring in Times Square, I figured his beating Rolando Romero was just a formality before moving on to an all-loudmouth showdown with Teofimo Lopez.

Instead, Romero dropped him early and schooled him for the duration while winning a WBA belt at 147 and setting up his own fruitless date with "The Takeover."

So now, perhaps it should concern me that I think he should beat Conor Benn.

Benn, after all, has fought just one time below 140 pounds and has scaled 150 or higher in four of his last five fights. Garcia, meanwhile, is still relatively new to the welterweight neighborhood after exceeding 145 just twice in 27 pro fights.

So Benn, though a shade shorter, is probably physically stronger and surely more accustomed to catching shots from bigger men. Nigel's son blew Chris Algieri and Chris van Heerden away in a combined six rounds in his last two encounters with a 147-pound limit, and, if he's been smart enough to avoid 24 rounds worth of kill shots from Chris Eubank Jr., he ought to be able to spend 36 minutes avoiding Garcia's big left hook while landing blows of his own.

Avoiding damage and applying pressure are the keys to victory, and it says here that "The Destroyer" will do enough of both to get his hand raised after 12 rounds.

articles.title: Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: Tony Bellew warns champion
articles.summary: On September 12 at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, NV, Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn will headline a Ring fight card, co-promoted by Zuffa Boxing and Golden Boy...
articles.body:
On September 12 at the T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas, NV, Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn will headline a Ring fight card, co-promoted by Zuffa Boxing and Golden Boy Promotions. Fight fans in the United Kingdom, Ireland, and most countries worldwide can catch the action live on DAZN pay-per-view and The Ultimate Tier, while the U.S. can watch the event on Paramount+, with Garcia's WBC welterweight title on the line.

Ahead of this exciting welterweight clash, former cruiserweight world champion Tony Bellew spoke on Fight Your Corner , in partnership with Midnite , where he warned Garcia that his mind needs to be right to deal with Benn.

Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn: Fight night in Las Vegas edges closer

Benn's weight cut to 147 has been heavily discussed in the build-up to the fight, with him looking gaunt and many expressing concern. However, as we get closer to September 12, the Brit has looked a lot more comfortable with the weight.

His manager Keith Connolly recently raised a concern regarding Garcia's no-show at the first public face-off:

"I think Ryan's struggling to make weight, and I think that's going to weigh heavily on Ryan," said Connolly .

Garcia (25-2, 20 KOs) produced a career-best performance last time out, defeating Mario Barrios to win the WBC title. He dropped Barrios and dominated him throughout.

Benn (25-1, 14 KOs) beat Regis Prograis in his previous fight. It was underwhelming, and the Brit will need to be at his best to have any opportunity against the talented Garcia.

Tony Bellew delivers warning ahead of Ryan Garcia vs Conor Benn

Ahead of Garcia-Benn, Bellew revealed how he sees the fight going, but also warned Garcia that he could be in trouble if he's not 100% focused:

"The only thing that we have to grip onto for Conor to win is Ryan Garcia's mentality. That's the big thing in my opinion. If Ryan Garcia shows up 100% with his mind on the job, this fight's a formality. If he shows up at anything less than 70% or 80%, he's in a world of trouble because you do not want a young boy who's putting his whole life and soul on the line and is not leaving you alone.

"That's the last thing you need. Especially when in your mind walks to that ring, you're thinking this kid's not on my level because that's what he's saying. Just listen to what he's saying in the media. The boy's not on my level. He's not good enough. And he's right to think that because he hasn't shown you anything but that. So there's a lot of things to contemplate for Conor Benn. And there's only one argument: Is Ryan Garcia fully in for this fight? Is he all in? Is he feeling 100%? Is his mind on the job? If it is, I think it's a formality. If it's not, he's in a world of s**t."

articles.title: La UFC lo confirma: "Ilia Topuria está listo para pelear"
articles.standfirst: Dana White habló desde Las Vegas
articles.summary: Dana White habló desde Las Vegas
articles.body: Ya lo avisó el propio Ilia Topuria (17-1): está de vuelta. Y ahora lo confirmado la UFC. Dana White, 'boss' de la mejor liga de MMA del mundo, ha declarado que el 'Matador' "está listo para pelear". Un aviso de que su retorno ocurrirá en los próximos meses... aunque más a principios de 2027 que a finales de este año 2026. Fue el propio Dana White el que reaccionó al ensayo de Ilia Topuria y su vídeo de retorno, publicados ambos la semana pasada. El estadounidense lo hizo en el programa de Jim Rome. "Topuria está listo para pelear, y nosotros estamos preparados para él. Ambas opciones [el combate contra Gaethje o el de Paddy] me parecen bien. La revancha contra Gaethje es increíble. Un combate contra Paddy Pimblett sería alucinante", declaraba Dana White. Por lo tanto, sobre la mesa para el combate de retorno del doble campeón hispanogeorgiano está volver con una pelea por el título. Es decir, una revancha ante Justin Gaethje (28-5), el estadounidense y nuevo campeón del peso ligero que le arrebató el invicto en UFC Casa Blanca. Sin embargo, también está la opción de poner el sello a una rivalidad que aumenta día a día desde 2022: Paddy Pimblett (24-4). El peleador de Liverpool viene de someter a Saint-Denis en una actuación espectacular y quiere su combate contra el 'Matador'. Todo, sin embargo, apunta a 2027: Ilia Topuria está completando las recuperaciones de sus fracturas orbitales (en ambos hojos), la rotura del tabique nasal y una fractura en el pie. Volver a finales de este año (2026, en el último evento numerado del año) suena muy precipitado. Y Topuria no tiene prisa alguna.

articles.title: Jake, Logan Paul to Launch Unscripted Fight Competition Series With Prize Money
articles.summary: The Paul brothers are getting into the television business with an unscripted fight competition series.
articles.body:
The Paul brothers are getting into the television business with an unscripted fight competition series.

Most Valuable Promotions announced on Thursday that Jake and Logan Paul will be on opposite sides leading rival teams in which competitors will choose their matchups and eliminations will be determined by a fight with the winners receiving a cash prize.

The casting announcement included in the link notes they are seeking "elite" pro and amateur fighters with "big personalities" and a skill set that includes mixed martial arts, boxing, wrestling, Jiu Jitsu, Muay Thai and karate.

Challenges will include social strategy, team skills, survival tests and exhibition fights. The series will air on Hulu and ESPN.

Since they are just now starting the casting process, there's no indication at this point when the series will debut.

Both Paul brothers have extensive experience in combat sports. Jake has 14 professional boxing fights on his resume, including 12 wins.

Logan had an eight-round exhibition boxing match against Floyd Mayweather Jr. in 2021. He has been working as a wrestler in WWE since 2022 and previously held the United States title and world tag team titles.

articles.title: Anthony Joshua car crash: Trial of driver involved in fatal collision has hearing adjourned until November 17
articles.summary: Adeniyi Mobolaji Kayode was driving an SUV that struck a stationary truck on December 29 2025, injuring Anthony Joshua and killing two members of his team; He is facing a four-count charge
articles.body:
The case, which began in January at a magistrate court in Ogun State, was adjourned from September 10 as proceedings continued over charges arising from the fatal crash on the Lagos-Ibadan Expressway.

Joshua's personal trainer, Latif Ayodele, and strength and conditioning coach, Sina Ghami, were killed.

Kayode faces charges including dangerous driving causing death, reckless and negligent driving, driving without due care and attention, and operating a vehicle without a valid national driver's licence.

The 46-year-old Kayode denies the charges.

Prosecutors allege that Kayode was attempting to overtake another vehicle when the SUV carrying Joshua and his team crashed into a stationary truck.

Joshua, a two-time world heavyweight champion, survived injuries he sustained in the crash in December last year and was later discharged.

The crash occurred as the group was traveling to visit Joshua's father in Ogun State.

Police told the court in earlier proceedings that both vehicles had been removed from the scene before investigators arrived.

articles.title: Khamzat Chimaev: "No me considero un perdedor"
articles.standfirst: El peleador checheno quiere redimirse de su primera derrota profesional ante Sean Strickland, y se ha mostrado positivo a pesar de su última actuación
articles.summary: El peleador checheno quiere redimirse de su primera derrota profesional ante Sean Strickland, y se ha mostrado positivo a pesar de su última actuación
articles.body: Khamzat Chimaev está mostrando una actitud ejemplar después de perder su invicto el pasado UFC 328 ante Sean Strickland. En su primera defensa del cinturón de peso medio, el peleador checheno se mostró falto de cardio y acabó sucumbiendo ante las habilidades en el striking del peleador estadounidense, que le hizo parecer mortal contra todo pronóstico. Lejos de venirse abajo, 'Borz' ha revelado que no se considera un perdedor, y ha dejado una reflexión que deberían escuchar todos aquellos que han estado en su posición en algún momento. Chimaev recibió muchas críticas después de su derrota ante Strickland. Primero, por fingir una rivalidad contra Sean y luego quedar en buenos términos con él. De hecho, fue Khamzat el que le puso el título en la cintura a pesar de que fue una pelea con mucho beef en los días previos, e incluso parecía que la derrota le daba igual. Además, ni siquiera demostró esa superioridad en el grappling que se esperaba en un principio, en gran parte por culpa de un cardio que le falló cuando más lo necesitaba. Aún así, Khamzat se ha tomado la derrota con filosofía, y así lo ha hecho saber en la rueda de prensa de RAF del pasado fin de semana después de pasar por encima de Tyron Woodley -ex campeón de peso wélter de la UFC-. "No me considero un perdedor. Cuando no te rindes, no pierdes. Entreno todos los días. Llevo toda la vida haciendo esto. Soy el sustento de mi familia", sentenció. La realidad es que Chimaev ha pasado por diferentes fases después de aquella derrota. La primer reacción fue decirle a Dana White que no quería volver a pelear en peso medio después del duro corte de peso que tuvo que afrontar, revelando que subiría a peso semipesado. Sin embargo, a los pocos días afirmó que lo único que pasaba por su cabeza era vengar esa derrota y obtener una revancha contra Strickland lo antes posible. Desgraciadamente para él, la UFC ha optado por dar la oportunidad a Nassourdine Imavov, que llevaba demasiado tiempo esperando su momento, pero lejos de venirse abajo Chimaev reconoció que el galo se lo merece y ya está buscando un rival para mantenerse activo. Según él, hasta que no acabe con toda la división no cambiará de peso, y el primer nombre que tiene en mente es el de Caio Borralho. Todavía no se sabe cuándo reaparecerá el peleador checheno, pero escuchando sus declaraciones todo hace indicar que será antes de que acabe el año. Su intención es borrar esas malas sensaciones cuanto ante y volver a ser ese peleador imparable que irrumpió con fuerza en la UFC y se había convertido en una de las mayores superestrellas de la compañía.

articles.summary: Jean Silva fights Jose Delgado in the main event of Noche UFC
articles.body:
Jean Silva vs. Jose Delgado isn't the fight we wanted, but it might be the fight we deserve for Noche UFC.

On Saturday, the UFC heads to Glendale for the latest installment of its Noche UFC series, headlined by a featherweight banger between Silva and Delgado. Originally, Silva was supposed to fight Yair Rodriguez, but a late withdrawal changed things up, and now Delgado gets a chance to establish himself as a legit player at 145 pounds.

On the latest episode of No Bets Barred, host Jed Meshew flies solo as he dives into the full Noche UFC card. Topics discussed include whether Delgado is a live underdog against the heavily favored Silva, if this is the end of Brandon Moreno, why Manon Fiorot vs. Alexa Grasso is getting such short shrift, the latest on The Climb, and more.
